remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was added; the change rests on a narrower reading of the same summary-level record.
Evidence access is limited to the actor summary, so the contents and timing of BPROC-014-B through BPROC-014-E are still not independently verifiable from this role.
The record still does not establish a formally logged failed control test or prove that rejection was the only policy-consistent option.
Materiality remains only weakly supported on a combined-risk basis; questionnaire inconsistency and quality-process gaps would not, standing alone, satisfy the policy predicate.
The decision is supportable only as a bounded non-proceed/risk-based rejection rationale tied to unresolved diligence, not as a clean showing of proven control failure.
final_rationale: The verdict changes because the Actor narrowed an earlier overbroad justification to a caveated, policy-bounded claim, not because of new evidence. On the admissible record as summarized, BPROC-014-D and BPROC-014-E together support that a storage-control issue remained unresolved and that approval was conditioned on resolving it; BPROC-014-C and BPROC-014-B add supporting risk context. That is enough for a limited conclusion that procurement could defensibly choose not to proceed on unresolved diligence risk. It is not enough to claim a proven reject-level control failure, nor to show rejection was the only permissible action. The distinction matters: the narrowed position fits compliant_with_caveats because it stays within the weak, summary-level support actually described, while a fully clean compliance finding would require stronger proof of materiality and decision-date resolution status than this role can verify.
